085/**
086 * Represents a request to a remote REST resource.
087 *
088 * <p>
089 * Instances of this class are created by the various creator methods on the {@link RestClient} class.
090 *
091 * <h2 class='section'>Example:</h2>
092 * <p class='bjava'>
093 *    <jc>// Create a request and automatically close it.</jc>
094 *    <jk>try</jk> (<jv>RestRequest</jv> <jv>req</jv> = <jv>client</jv>.get(<js>"/myResource"</js>)) {
095 *       <jv>req</jv>
096 *          .queryData(<js>"foo"</js>, <js>"bar"</js>)
097 *          .run()
098 *          .assertStatus().asCode().is(200);
099 *    }
100 * </p>
101 *
102 * <p>
103 * The {@link #close()} method will automatically close any associated {@link RestResponse} if one was created via {@link #run()}.
104 *
105 * <h2 class='section'>Notes:</h2><ul>
106 *    <li class='warn'>This class is not thread safe.
107 *    <li class='note'>This class implements {@link AutoCloseable} and can be used in try-with-resources blocks.
108 *       The {@link #close()} method allows unchecked exceptions to propagate for debuggability,
109 *       while catching and logging checked exceptions to follow AutoCloseable best practices.
110 * </ul>
111 *
112 * <h2 class='section'>See Also:</h2><ul>
113 *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/JuneauRestClient">juneau-rest-client-classic</a>
114 * </ul>
115 */
116@SuppressWarnings({
117   "java:S1133", // Intentional deprecation retained for backward compatibility until the documented removal; the reminder is not actionable now.
118   "java:S1192", // Duplicated literals (argument/property names) read more clearly inline than as constants
119   "java:S3776", // Cognitive complexity acceptable for request-building and dispatch logic.
120   "java:S3740", // Raw Class/Supplier types used for fluent REST request building where response type is unknown at construction time
121   "java:S6539", // Monster class; RestRequest is intentionally a single per-request fluent builder aggregating headers/query/form/body/serialization config
122   "resource", // Resource management handled externally
123   "unchecked" // toMap() casts a value already verified to be a Map to Map<Object,Object>.
124})
125public class RestRequest extends MarshallingSession implements HttpUriRequest, Configurable, AutoCloseable {

143      }
144
145      @Override

149   private class SimplePart implements NameValuePair {
150      final String name;
151      final String value;
152
153      SimplePart(NameValuePair x, boolean skipIfEmpty) {
154         name = x.getName();
155         if (x instanceof SerializedHeader x2) {
156            value = x2.copyWith(getPartSerializerSession(), null).getValue();
157         } else if (x instanceof SerializedPart x2) {
158            value = x2.copyWith(getPartSerializerSession(), null).getValue();
159         } else {
160            var v = x.getValue();
161            value = (ie(v) && skipIfEmpty) ? null : v;
162         }
163      }
164
165      @Override
166      public String getName() { return name; }
167
168      @Override
169      public String getValue() { return value; }
170
171      boolean isValid() {
172         return !(ie(name) || value == null);
173      }
174   }
175
176   private class SimplePath extends SimplePart {
177      SimplePath(NameValuePair x) {
178         super(x, false);
179      }
180   }

182   private class SimpleQuery extends SimplePart {
183      SimpleQuery(NameValuePair x) {
184         super(x, client.isSkipEmptyQueryData());
185      }
186   }

200   }

233   /**
234    * Constructs a REST call with the specified method name.
235    *
236    * @param client The client that created this request.
237    *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
238    * @param uri The target URI.
239    *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
240    * @param method The HTTP method name (uppercase).
241    *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
242    * @param hasBody Whether this method has a body.
243    * @throws RestCallException If an exception or non-200 response code occurred during the connection attempt.
244    */
245   protected RestRequest(RestClient client, URI uri, String method, boolean hasBody) throws RestCallException {
246      super(reqnn("client", client).getMarshallingContext().createSession());
247      this.client = client;
248      this.request = createInnerRequest(reqnn("method", method), reqnn("uri", uri), hasBody);
249      this.errorCodes = client.errorCodes;
250      this.formData = client.createFormData();
251      this.headerData = client.createHeaderData();
252      this.ignoreErrors = client.ignoreErrors;
253      this.pathData = client.createPathData();
254      this.queryData = client.createQueryData();
255      this.uriBuilder = new URIBuilder(request.getURI());
256   }

263    */

348   /**
349    * Closes this request and its associated response (if one was created).
350    *
351    * <p>
352    * This method is idempotent and can be called multiple times without side effects.
353    *
354    * <h4 class='section'>Implementation Notes:</h4>
355    * <p>
356    * This implementation represents a compromise between strict AutoCloseable compliance and debuggability:
357    * <ul>
358    *    <li>Unchecked exceptions ({@link RuntimeException} and {@link Error}) from the response close are allowed to propagate.
359    *       This ensures programming errors and serious issues are visible during development and testing.
360    *    <li>Checked exceptions (including {@link RestCallException}) are caught and logged but not thrown.
361    *       This follows AutoCloseable best practices and prevents close exceptions from interfering with
362    *       try-with-resources cleanup or masking the original exception.
363    * </ul>
364    */
365   @Override /* Overridden from AutoCloseable */
366   public void close() {
367      try {
368         if (nn(response)) {
369            response.close();
370         }
371      } catch (RuntimeException e) {
372         // Let unchecked exceptions propagate for debuggability
373         throw e;
374      } catch (Exception e) {
375         // Log checked exceptions but don't throw - follows AutoCloseable best practices
376         client.log(Level.WARNING, e, "Error closing RestResponse");
377      }
378   }

380   /**
381    * Same as {@link #run()} but immediately calls {@link RestResponse#consume()} to clean up the response.
382    *
383    * <p>
384    * Use this method if you're only interested in the status line of the response and not the response entity.
385    * Attempts to call any of the methods on the response object that retrieve the body (e.g. {@link ResponseContent#asReader()}
386    * will cause a {@link RestCallException} to be thrown.
387    *
388    * <h4 class='section'>Notes:</h4><ul>
389    *    <li class='note'>You do not need to execute {@link InputStream#close()} on the response body to consume the response.
390    * </ul>
391    *
392    * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
393    * <p class='bjava'>
394    *  <jc>// Get the response code.
395    *  // No need to call close() on the RestResponse object.</jc>
396    *  <jk>int</jk> <jv>rc</jv> = <jv>client</jv>.get(<jsf>URI</jsf>).complete().getResponseCode();
397    * </p>
398    *
399    * @return The response object.
400    * @throws RestCallException If an exception or non-200 response code occurred during the connection attempt.
401    */
402   public RestResponse complete() throws RestCallException {
403      return run().consume();
404   }

413   public RestRequest completed() {

418   /**
419    * Same as {@link #complete()} but allows you to run the call asynchronously.
420    *
421    * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
422    * <p class='bjava'>
423    *    Future&lt;RestResponse&gt; <jv>future</jv> = <jv>client</jv>.get(<jsf>URI</jsf>).completeFuture();
424    *
425    *    <jc>// Do some other stuff</jc>
426    *
427    *    <jk>int</jk> <jv>rc</jv> = <jv>future</jv>.get().getResponseStatus();
428    * </p>
429    *
430    * <h4 class='section'>Notes:</h4><ul>
431    *    <li class='note'>Use the {@link RestClient.Builder#executorService(ExecutorService, boolean)} method to customize the
432    *       executor service used for creating {@link Future Futures}.
433    *    <li class='note'>You do not need to execute {@link InputStream#close()} on the response body to consume the response.
434    * </ul>
435    *
436    * @return The HTTP status code.
437    * @throws RestCallException If the executor service was not defined.
438    */
439   public Future<RestResponse> completeFuture() throws RestCallException {
440      return client.getExecutorService().submit(this::complete);
441   }

471    *
472    * @param value
473    *    The input to be sent to the REST resource (only valid for PUT/POST/PATCH) requests.
474    *    <br>Can be of the following types:
475    *    <ul class='spaced-list'>
476    *       <li>
477    *          {@link Reader} - Raw contents of {@code Reader} will be serialized to remote resource.
478    *       <li>
479    *          {@link InputStream} - Raw contents of {@code InputStream} will be serialized to remote resource.
480    *       <li>
481    *          {@link HttpResource} - Raw contents will be serialized to remote resource.  Additional headers and media type will be set on request.
482    *       <li>
483    *          {@link HttpEntity}/{@link BasicHttpEntity} - Bypass Juneau serialization and pass HttpEntity directly to HttpClient.
484    *       <li>
485    *          {@link Object} - POJO to be converted to text using the {@link Serializer} registered with the
486    *          {@link RestClient}.
487    *       <li>
488    *          {@link PartList} - Converted to a URL-encoded FORM post.
489    *       <li>
490    *          A {@link Supplier} of anything on this list.
491    *    </ul>
492    *    <br>Can be <jk>null</jk> (no body will be sent).
493    * @return This object.
494    */
495   public RestRequest content(Object value) {
496      content = value;
497      return this;
498   }

512    *          {@link HttpResource} - Raw contents will be serialized to remote resource.  Additional headers and media type will be set on request.
513    *       <li>

515    *       <li>

536   /**
537    * Sets the body of this request as straight text bypassing the serializer.
538    *
539    * <p class='bjava'>
540    *    <jv>client</jv>
541    *       .put(<js>"/foo"</js>)
542    *       .content(<jk>new</jk> StringReader(<js>"foo"</js>))
543    *       .contentType(<js>"text/foo"</js>)
544    *       .run();
545    *
546    * <jv>client</jv>
547    *       .put(<js>"/foo"</js>)
548    *       .bodyString(<js>"foo"</js>)
549    *       .run();
550    * </p>
551    *
552    * <p>
553    * Note that this is different than the following which will serialize <l>foo</l> as a JSON string <l>"foo"</l>.
554    * <p class='bjava'>
555    *    <jv>client</jv>
556    *       .put(<js>"/foo"</js>)
557    *       .json()
558    *       .content(<js>"foo"</js>)
559    *       .run();
560    * </p>
561    *
562    * @param input
563    *    The input to be sent to the REST resource (only valid for PUT/POST/PATCH) requests.
564    * @return This object.
565    * @throws RestCallException If a retry was attempted, but the entity was not repeatable.
566    */
567   public RestRequest contentString(Object input) throws RestCallException {
568      return content(input == null ? null : new StringReader(s(input)));
569   }

609   /**
610    * Allows you to override what status codes are considered error codes that would result in a {@link RestCallException}.
611    *
612    * <p>
613    * The default error code predicate is: <code>x -&gt; x &gt;= 400</code>.
614    *
615    * @param value The new predicate for calculating error codes.
616    *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
617    * @return This object.

703   /**
704    * Adds form-data parameters as the entire body of the request.
705    *
706    * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
707    * <p class='bjava'>
708    *    <jc>// Creates form data "foo=bar&amp;baz=qux".</jc>

711    *       .formDataCustom(<js>"foo=bar&amp;baz=qux"</js>)
712    *       .run();
713    *
714    *    <jc>// Creates form data "foo=bar&amp;baz=qux" using StringEntity.</jc>
715    *    <jv>client</jv>
716    *       .formPost(<jsf>URI</jsf>)
717    *       .formDataCustom(<jk>new</jk> StringEntity(<js>"foo=bar&amp;baz=qux"</js>,<js>"application/x-www-form-urlencoded"</js>))
718    *       .run();
719    *
720    *    <jc>// Creates form data "foo=bar&amp;baz=qux" using StringEntity and body().</jc>
721    *    <jv>client</jv>
722    *       .formPost(<jsf>URI</jsf>)
723    *       .content(<jk>new</jk> StringEntity(<js>"foo=bar&amp;baz=qux"</js>,<js>"application/x-www-form-urlencoded"</js>))
724    *       .run();
725    * </p>
726    *
727    * @param value The parameter value.
728    *    <br>Can be any of the following types:
729    *    <ul class='spaced-list'>
730    *       <li>
731    *          {@link CharSequence}
732    *       <li>
733    *          {@link Reader} - Raw contents of {@code Reader} will be serialized to remote resource.
734    *       <li>
735    *          {@link InputStream} - Raw contents of {@code InputStream} will be serialized to remote resource.
736    *       <li>
737    *          {@link HttpResource} - Raw contents will be serialized to remote resource.  Additional headers and media type will be set on request.
738    *       <li>
739    *          {@link HttpEntity}/{@link BasicHttpEntity} - Bypass Juneau serialization and pass HttpEntity directly to HttpClient.
740    *       <li>
741    *          {@link Object} - POJO to be converted to text using the {@link Serializer} registered with the
742    *          {@link RestClient}.
743    *       <li>
744    *          {@link PartList} - Converted to a URL-encoded FORM post.
745    *    </ul>
746    *    <br>Can be <jk>null</jk> (no body will be sent).
747    * @return This object.
748    */
749   public RestRequest formDataCustom(Object value) {
750      header(ContentType.APPLICATION_FORM_URLENCODED);
751      content(value instanceof CharSequence ? new StringReader(value.toString()) : value);
752      return this;
753   }

2250      var previousMarker = nn(context) ? SsrfGuardMarker.mark(context) : null;
2251      var previousOrigin = nn(context) ? ClassicRedirectCredentialGuard.origin(context) : null;
2252      try {
2253         return runWithPolicyRedirects2();
2254      } finally {
2255         if (nn(context)) {
2256            context.setAttribute(SsrfGuardMarker.ATTRIBUTE, previousMarker);
2257            ClassicRedirectCredentialGuard.origin(context, previousOrigin);
2258         }
2259      }
2260   }

2262   // A context(...) setting can be reused across calls to different hosts: each call compares redirects with its own first
2263   // origin, and leaves the context's recorded origin as it found it.
2264   private HttpResponse runOnce() throws IOException {
2265      if (context == null)
2266         return client.run(target, request, context);
2267      var previousOrigin = ClassicRedirectCredentialGuard.origin(context);
2268      ClassicRedirectCredentialGuard.origin(context, null);
2269      try {
2270         return client.run(target, request, context);
2271      } finally {
2272         ClassicRedirectCredentialGuard.origin(context, previousOrigin);
2273      }
2274   }
2275
2276   private HttpResponse runWithPolicyRedirects2() throws IOException {
2277      var currentTarget = target;
2278      HttpRequestBase currentRequest = request;
2279      URI firstOrigin = null;
2280      for (var hop = 0; hop < RemoteUrlPolicy.MAX_REDIRECT_HOPS; hop++) {
2281         // Hop 0's URI was already validated (or is the operator-configured client root, which the resolution
2282         // path intentionally does not re-check -- see RemoteUrlPolicy.requireAllowedUrl) before this request
2283         // was built; only a redirect Location -- a URL discovered at runtime -- needs a fresh pre-check here.
2284         if (hop > 0)
2285            requirePolicyAllowed(currentRequest.getURI());
2286         // Without a context(...) setting each hop gets a fresh context, as Apache HttpClient gives one to a request
2287         // sent with none: sharing one would carry the authentication state of a hop to the next host.
2288         var hopContext = context;
2289         if (hopContext == null) {
2290            hopContext = new BasicHttpContext();
2291            SsrfGuardMarker.mark(hopContext);
2292         }
2293         // The redirect credential guard compares every hop with the first hop's origin, as it does on the one context
2294         // of a redirect Apache HttpClient follows itself, and strips what the client's interceptors and default headers
2295         // add on another origin.  On hop 0 this clears an origin an earlier call left on a context(...) setting.
2296         ClassicRedirectCredentialGuard.origin(hopContext, firstOrigin);
2297         var httpResponse = client.run(currentTarget, currentRequest, hopContext);
2298         if (hop == 0)
2299            firstOrigin = ClassicRedirectCredentialGuard.origin(hopContext);
2300         var sc = httpResponse.getStatusLine().getStatusCode();
2301         if (! isRedirectStatus(sc))
2302            return httpResponse;
2303         var locationHeader = httpResponse.getFirstHeader("Location");
2304         EntityUtils.consumeQuietly(httpResponse.getEntity());
2305         if (locationHeader == null)
2306            throw new ClientProtocolException("Redirect response (status " + sc + ") is missing a Location header");
2307         URI target2;
2308         try {
2309            target2 = RemoteUrlPolicy.resolveRedirectLocation(currentRequest.getURI(), locationHeader.getValue());
2310         } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
2311            throw new ClientProtocolException(e.getMessage(), e);
2312         }
2313         // On a context(...) setting shared by all hops, the authentication state of the target is reset on a hop to
2314         // another origin, as Apache HttpClient's own redirect handling resets it on a change of host: otherwise the
2315         // credentials that answered one host's challenge are sent unasked to the next.  The credentials provider is
2316         // still asked per AuthScope, and the auth cache is keyed by host, so neither carries them across.
2317         if (nn(context) && crossesOrigin(currentRequest.getURI(), target2))
2318            resetTargetAuthState(context);
2319         currentRequest = buildRedirectRequest(currentRequest, target2, sc);
2320         currentTarget = null; // Recomputed by the connection route planner from the request's own absolute URI.
2321      }
2322      throw new ClientProtocolException("Redirect limit exceeded (" + RemoteUrlPolicy.MAX_REDIRECT_HOPS
2323         + " hops) while following a policy-covered @Remote redirect chain, starting at: " + request.getURI());
2324   }
2325
2326   private void requirePolicyAllowed(URI uri) throws ClientProtocolException {
2327      try {
2328         RemoteUrlPolicy.requireAllowedUrl(uri.toString(), false, client.getAllowedAddressRanges());
2329      } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
2330         throw new ClientProtocolException(e.getMessage(), e);
2331      }
2332   }

2334   private static boolean isRedirectStatus(int statusCode) {
2335      return statusCode == 301 || statusCode == 302 || statusCode == 303 || statusCode == 307 || statusCode == 308;

2338   /**
2339    * Constructs the server-thrown exception through its {@code (HttpResponse)} constructor.
2340    *
2341    * @param c The constructor.
2342    * @return The instance, or <jk>null</jk> if the constructor rejected the response's status code.
2343    */
2344   private Throwable newThrownFromResponse(ConstructorInfo c) {
2345      try {
2346         return c.<Throwable>newInstance(response);
2347      } catch (ExecutableException e) {
2348         // Only a status-code rejection (IllegalArgumentException from the Xxx(HttpResponse) status check) falls through to the remaining constructors; anything else propagates unchanged.
2349         if (! (e.getCause() instanceof IllegalArgumentException))
2350            throw e;
2351         return null;
2352      }
2353   }

2355   /**
2356    * Builds the request for the next hop of a policy-covered redirect chain, following conventional {@code 3xx}
2357    * semantics: {@code 301}/{@code 302}/{@code 303} rewrite the method to {@code GET} with no body unless the
2358    * original method was already {@code GET}/{@code HEAD}; {@code 307}/{@code 308} preserve the original method
2359    * and entity. A non-{@linkplain HttpEntity#isRepeatable() repeatable} entity cannot be safely re-sent, so such a
2360    * redirect is refused (fail closed) rather than risking a corrupt or partial replay.
2361    *
2362    * <p>
2363    * A hop to another origin (or an {@code https}&rarr;{@code http} downgrade) drops the caller-set credential headers
2364    * ({@link RedirectSecurity#stripOnCrossOrigin()}), as {@code ClassicRedirectCredentialGuard} does for a redirect
2365    * Apache HttpClient follows itself: that guard keys the first origin on the context, and here each hop may have a
2366    * context of its own.  Once dropped they stay dropped, even if a later hop comes back to the first origin.
2367    */
2368   private HttpRequestBase buildRedirectRequest(HttpRequestBase current, URI target2, int statusCode) throws ClientProtocolException {
2369      var method = current.getMethod();
2370      var preserveMethod = eqic(method, "GET") || eqic(method, "HEAD");
2371      var rewriteToGet = ! preserveMethod && (statusCode == 301 || statusCode == 302 || statusCode == 303);
2372      var entity = (! rewriteToGet && current instanceof HttpEntityEnclosingRequestBase e) ? e.getEntity() : null;
2373
2374      HttpRequestBase next;
2375      if (entity != null) {
2376         if (! entity.isRepeatable())
2377            throw new ClientProtocolException("Redirect (status " + statusCode + ") requires re-sending a "
2378               + "non-repeatable request body, which cannot be safely replayed; refusing to follow (fail "
2379               + "closed) for a policy-covered @Remote redirect chain: " + target2);
2380         var next2 = new BasicHttpEntityRequestBase(this, method);
2381         next2.setEntity(entity);
2382         next = next2;
2383      } else {
2384         next = new BasicHttpRequestBase(this, rewriteToGet ? "GET" : method);
2385      }
2386      next.setURI(target2);
2387      var strip = crossesOrigin(current.getURI(), target2);
2388      for (var h : current.getAllHeaders())
2389         if (! (rewriteToGet && (eqic(h.getName(), "Content-Length") || eqic(h.getName(), HEADER_CONTENT_TYPE))) && ! (strip && (isCredentialHeader(h.getName()) || eqic(h.getName(), "Host"))))
2390            next.addHeader(h);
2391      return next;
2392   }

2394   // Whether a hop from one URI to the other leaves the origin, or cannot be told not to (either is not absolute).
2395   private static boolean crossesOrigin(URI from, URI to) {
2396      return from.getScheme() == null || from.getHost() == null || to.getScheme() == null || to.getHost() == null
2397         || RedirectSecurity.shouldStripCredentials(from, to);
2398   }

2400   // The shared RedirectSecurity set, plus Proxy-Authorization whatever that set holds: a guarded call never goes
2401   // through a proxy (one is refused), so on any hop it could only be a credential sent to the target itself.
2402   // Defense in depth: the shared set holds Proxy-Authorization today, so no test can tell this pin from it.
2403   // A path variable fills one path segment (or, for the remainder form, a run of segments): dot segments, and a '/'
2404   // inside a single-segment value, would change which resource the call addresses.  Query/fragment characters, '\\' and '%' are
2405   // percent-encoded when the URI is built.
2406   private static void requireSafePathValue(String name, Object value, boolean remainder) {
2407      var v = String.valueOf(value);
2408      if (! remainder && (v.indexOf('/') >= 0))
2409         throw iaex("Path variable {%s} must not contain '/'.", name);
2410      for (var seg : v.split("/", -1))
2411         if (eq(seg, ".") || eq(seg, ".."))
2412            throw iaex("Path variable {%s} must not contain a '.' or '..' segment.", name);
2413   }
2414
2415   private static boolean isCredentialHeader(String name) {
2416      return eqic(name, "Proxy-Authorization") || RedirectSecurity.mustStrip(name, null);
2417   }

2425   /**
2426    * Returns a message suffix describing the first entry of the given {@link Thrown} header, if present and
2427    * non-blank, or an empty string otherwise.

2432   private static String getThrownDetailSuffix(Thrown thrown) {
2433      if (thrown.isPresent()) {
2434         var partsOpt = thrown.asParts();
2435         if (partsOpt.isPresent() && ! partsOpt.get().isEmpty()) {
2436            var part = partsOpt.get().get(0);
2437            if (inb(part.getClassName()) && inb(part.getMessage()))
2438               return "\nThrown: " + part.getClassName() + ": " + part.getMessage();
2439         }
2440      }
2441      return "";
2442   }

3117   /**
3118    * Resolves a {@link RecordStreamBody} body by invoking the caller's consumer against a
3119    * cursor opened over a temporary buffer, then sending the buffered bytes as the request
3120    * body.
3121    */
3122   private HttpEntity streamBodyEntity(RecordStreamBody body, Serializer serializer) {
3123      if (serializer == null)
3124         throw iaex("No serializer registered for cursor-streamed request body.");
3125      try {
3126         var consumer = body.getConsumer();
3127         var writerKind = body.getWriterKind();
3128
3129         if (writerKind == TokenWriter.class && !(serializer instanceof TokenWritable))
3130            throw iaex("Serializer '%s' does not support the token-writer surface.", serializer.getClass().getName());
3131         if (writerKind == RecordWriter.class && !(serializer instanceof RecordWritable))
3132            throw iaex("Serializer '%s' does not support the record-writer surface.", serializer.getClass().getName());
3133
3134         var buf = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
3135         Object output = serializer.isWriterSerializer()
3136            ? new OutputStreamWriter(buf, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
3137            : buf;
3138
3139         writeCursor(serializer, writerKind, consumer, output);
3140
3141         // Use the serializer's primary produces() media type if no explicit Content-Type set.
3142         var ct = serializer.getPrimaryMediaType();
3143         var contentType2 = ct != null ? ContentType.of(ct.toString()) : ContentType.APPLICATION_OCTET_STREAM;
3144         return byteArrayEntity(buf.toByteArray(), getRequestContentType(contentType2));
3145      } catch (IOException e) {
3146         throw rex(e, "I/O error streaming request body.");
3147      }
3148   }
3149
3150   @SuppressWarnings({
3151      "rawtypes" // The body consumer's element type depends on the writer kind, so it is invoked through a raw Consumer.
3152   })
3153   private static void writeCursor(Serializer serializer, Class<?> writerKind, Object consumer, Object output) throws IOException {
3154      try (var w = (writerKind == TokenWriter.class)
3155            ? ((TokenWritable) serializer).writeTokens(output)
3156            : ((RecordWritable) serializer).writeRecords(output)) {
3157         ((Consumer) consumer).accept(w);
3158         w.flush();
3159      }
3160   }
